(DB2, Oracle, SQL Server).  We have just recently gotten our Hadoop
cluster prototype up and running, and we are using the Cloudera
'sqoop' tool to migrate very small subsets of that data to HDFS.

and so we have not yet made a significant data migration to HDFS.

messages.subject: Re: [rhipe] "subprocess failed with code 139"
messages.body_plain:
Hello,
I figured out why. The RHIPE C program writes a startup message to a log file
/tmp/logger. Now I guess you ran some code first (and you can check permissions
as to who owns it : ls -l /tmp/logger) and then another person with a different
UID runs a mr job and RHIPE tries writing to this log files and fails.

So, you can
a) delete the log file (tedious)
b) download (yet again) from
http://ml.stat.purdue.edu/rhipe/dn/Rhipe_0.51.tar.gz

and install across the worker nodes. It should now work for both local
and non local jobs.

The new version creates a log file called /tmp/logger-UID where UID is the
effective UID of the user.

It should work now(tested with two different users, though for me Hadoop has
issues running local jobs for different users but I guess thats due to my
cranky setup)

BTW, every run adds a few lines to the log file (/tmp/logger-UID
replace UID with users UID) and does not perform any log rotation, so
after several jobs it might grow large ..(but hardly so)
Soon, I'll insert code for log rotation.
Regards
Saptarshi

On Dec 2, 12:42 pm, Saptarshi Guha <saptarshi.g...@gmail.com> wrote:
> Hello,
> I figured out why. The RHIPE C program writes a startup message to a log file
> /tmp/logger. Now I guess you ran some code first (and you can check permissions
> as to who owns it : ls -l /tmp/logger) and then another person with a different
> UID runs a mr job and RHIPE tries writing to this log files and fails.
>
> So, you can
> a) delete the log file (tedious)

> b) download (yet again) fromhttp://ml.stat.purdue.edu/rhipe/dn/Rhipe_0.51.tar.gz <http://ml.stat.purdue.edu/rhipe/dn/Rhipe_0.51.tar.gz>

>
> and install across the worker nodes. It should now work for both local
> and non local jobs.
>
> The new version creates a log file called /tmp/logger-UID where UID is the
> effective UID of the user.
>
> It should work now(tested with two different users, though for me Hadoop has
> issues running local jobs for different users but I guess thats due to my
> cranky setup)
>
> BTW, every run adds a few lines to the log file (/tmp/logger-UID
> replace UID with users UID) and does not perform any log rotation, so
> after several jobs it might grow large ..(but hardly so)
> Soon, I'll insert code for log rotation.
> Regards
> Saptarshi

messages.subject: Version 0.52 - rhcounter more robust
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

In versions before 0.52 (latest), a "," in the group or subgroup of
rhcounter would upset Hadoop to the point the job would fail.

This version fixes this.

If you don't want to upgrade, a workaround is not to use "," in the
first two parameters of rhcounter. For details about rhcounter see [1]
and [2]

Download site: http://ml.stat.purdue.edu/rhipe/#sec-5

Regards
Saptarshi

[1] http://ml.stat.purdue.edu/rhipe/doc/html/rhmr.html#counter
[2] From http://www.umiacs.umd.edu/~jimmylin/cloud9/docs/content/counters.html

"
Built-In Counters

Counters are lightweight objects in Hadoop that allow you to keep track of
system progress in both the map and reduce stages of processing. By
default, Hadoop defines a number of standard counters in "groups";
these show up in the jobtracker Webapp, giving you information such as
"Map input records", "Map output records", etc.
"
